content.text: The small catalog is intentional in the current code, not a refresh bug: it is filtered to four hard-coded transports, and native has no persisted voice/image/video model configuration at all.

Audit complete — mobile’s small provider list is deliberate, caused by transport constraints.

- `ProviderId` is a closed union of `openai | anthropic | google | openrouter | custom` in [types.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/types.ts:1).
- `MODELS_DEV_PROVIDERS` hard-codes exactly those four cloud providers; every other models.dev provider is discarded before model parsing in [model-catalog.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog.ts:55) and [model-catalog.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog.ts:147).
- It then rejects every non-text output plus specially named realtime/TTS/image/audio/video models in [model-catalog.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog.ts:61) and [model-catalog.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/model-catalog.ts:165).
- Native execution only implements four wire protocols: OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini GenerateContent, and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions ([provider-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-client.ts:165)). Adding providers to the picker without a route/auth adapter would create selections that cannot run.
- Settings repeats the same five provider cards ([provider-config.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/provider-config.ts:12), [settings.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:235)); keys are likewise typed to that union ([storage.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/storage.ts:13)).

The Tutor selector location is already correct: it opens from the header and Composer model action ([index.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:213), [index.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/index.tsx:322)). It has search, multi-provider filters, all-capability AND filtering, recents, cache, and refresh ([ModelSelectorSheet.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/ModelSelectorSheet.tsx:71)). What is missing is provider breadth and modality-aware catalogs.

Web comparison:
- Web’s chat picker does **not** use models.dev directly. It loads all providers supplied by `pi-ai`, then custom providers and MiniMax compatibility entries ([provider-models.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:459)); it offers search/provider/capability filters ([ModelSelector.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/ModelSelector.tsx:199)).
- Web has separate fixed image-generator choices, currently OpenAI or local OpenAI-compatible — not a general models.dev image picker ([image-generators.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/lib/image-generators.ts:29)).
- Web separately persists speech provider/model/voice, mic/video preferences ([speech.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/speech.ts:44)), with four concrete registered speech transports: Gemini Live, OpenAI TTS, OpenAI Realtime, Supertonic ([speech.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/speech.ts:457)).
- Mobile has none of those media settings or transports; Live explicitly hands off to web ([live.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/live.tsx:27)).

Recommended dependency-safe implementation:

1. Replace the closed provider catalog with dynamic catalog records:
   `providerId: string`, display metadata, modality sets, limits/reasoning, and an explicit `execution` state: `native`, `configured-gateway`, or `setup-required`.
2. Parse and cache all models.dev providers/models for discovery. Preserve `modalities.input` and `.output` rather than reducing them to `vision`; do not use name regexes as the modality classifier.
3. Keep selection truthful: all models can be found and inspected, but Tutor only enables models with an executable configured transport. For others, selection opens a provider setup sheet—endpoint, supported wire API, key—and never produces a false “configured” state.
4. Generalize credentials to `providerId: string`; migrate existing SecureStore names unchanged. Persist a dynamic `ProviderConnection` with base URL, wire API, key reference, enabled status, and optional custom headers—not raw keys in AsyncStorage.
5. Add a transport registry before broad execution support. Start with OpenAI-compatible gateways and existing native OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini routes; add provider-specific adapters only where their actual endpoint semantics differ. The existing request builder cannot safely infer this from models.dev metadata alone.
6. Split feature selections from chat:
   - `chatModel`
   - `imageGenerationModel`
   - `voiceModel` plus voice name and TTS/realtime capability
   - `videoGenerationModel`, distinct from a live video-input model.
   
   Use the same searchable sheet and provider filters, but constrain each by advertised modality *and* executable feature transport.
7. Implement media transports and permissions before enabling their pickers: image generation endpoint, TTS/realtime audio, video generation, and live camera/video input are different contracts. Mobile’s current `KeatingUiSettings` has only theme/font/cards/errors/reasoning ([ui-settings.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/ui-settings.ts:19)).
8. Tests should cover all-provider retention, modality filtering, unsupported-but-discoverable setup states, migration/key isolation, route-specific request bodies, and that unavailable media selections cannot initiate a request.

Current tests encode the restrictive behavior—e.g. unsupported providers and non-chat models are expected to disappear ([model-catalog.test.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/test/model-catalog.test.ts:59)). Those assertions must be intentionally replaced, not worked around.

models.dev itself documents separate provider, canonical-model, and combined-catalog JSON endpoints; its metadata is appropriate for discovery, but it is not an execution/authentication contract. [Models.dev API documentation](https://models.dev/)
